## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One critical defect needs fixing first. `requirement_proven([])` now returns `True`, so a requirement with no criteria is reported as proven, and the old code returned `False` for that input. This review read the full pinned diff, all of `app/proof.py` and `tests/test_proof.py`, and searched the repository for callers. The policy manifest lists no policy files. `reviewed_batch` rejects an empty batch with a clear `ValueError`, and its added test covers the empty, all-reviewed and mixed cases.

## Changes
The pull request rewrites `requirement_proven` to compare a sum of `proven` flags against the number of criteria. It also adds a `reviewed_batch` helper that raises on an empty batch and checks that every entry is reviewed, plus a `REVIEW_HINT` module constant and a new test file.

## Critical
- app/proof.py:3 — correctness — Return False for an empty criteria list — With `criteria=[]`, `proven` is `0` and `len(criteria)` is `0`, so `proven == len(criteria)` returns `True`. The removed line `bool(criteria) and all(...)` returned `False` for the same input. No test calls `requirement_proven([])`, so the added tests do not catch this. — A requirement with no criteria or evidence now reports as proven, which defeats the purpose of a proof summary. It also conflicts with `reviewed_batch` in the same diff, which treats an empty input as invalid. — Fix: Restore the empty-list guard, for example `return bool(criteria) and all(item["proven"] for item in criteria)`, and add an assertion that `requirement_proven([])` is falsy to `tests/test_proof.py`.
